source_text: faex sellulariorum, in nos concitata; milites; scholasticos in auditoriis; nautas, tabernarios, cetarios, coquos, laniatores; iuvenes a monachis avulsos; de turba clericorum omnis generis, quia non possunt secundum categorias Aristotelis de dogmatibus iudicare; denegari nobis examinationem et iudicium episcoporum
pass_a_gloss: Faex sellulariorum, in we concitata; milites; scholasticos in auditoriis; nautas, tabernarios, cetarios, coquos, laniatores; iuvenes from monachis avulsos; about/from turba of-clergy all generis, because not are-able according-to categories of-Aristotle about/from doctrines iudicare; denegari to-us examination and judgment episcoporum.
pass_b_english: “The common dregs of sedentary tradesmen,” “stirred up against us.”
“Soldiers”; “students in lecture halls”; “sailors, shopkeepers, fishmongers, cooks, butchers”; “young men who have broken away from the monks.”
“From a crowd of all sorts of clergy,” “because they cannot judge doctrines according to Aristotle’s categories.”
“We are denied an examination and a judgment by bishops.”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
